turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided on that zero, and when?
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
You'll have my position in writing. Right now it's the zero coming off and an apology. Who decided, Hale?
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
You're asking me to negotiate against myself before you've shown me anything. The zero comes off. Was Owen heard before it went in?
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
That's your job, not mine. You called this meeting, so you must have brought something. Put it on the table.
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
Show it to me and find out. Is there an outline, or are we still talking about what I might say?
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
I won't agree to my son being punished on a machine's guess. That's four questions about me and nothing about Owen's essay. What do you have, Hale?
